items.title: US midterms today as Iran offers to reopen Hormuz on strict conditions
items.summary: US midterm elections are scheduled for 3 November. Reports from 2 November say Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, including sanctions relief and release of frozen assets, which Washington is unlikely to accept, and that oil fell sharply on Monday on hopes of a deal. Several reports also say a new US operation against Iran could follow soon after the vote; that is unconfirmed and provisional.
items.why: Gulf diplomacy and US politics drive oil prices, which feed into corporate budgets, hiring and marketing spend.
items.src: Yahoo News, CBS News, Times of Israel

items.title: Ukraine and Russia both said their emergency alert apps were hacked overnight
items.summary: A search summary says both countries reported false air-raid, chemical and nuclear warnings sent through their alert apps, and that Ukrainian emergency services said a Russian strike on a school in Zaporizhzhia region killed 24 people on Monday. These come from a single aggregated summary, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: A reminder of how crisis communication and trust in official channels can be attacked.

items.title: Rupee steadies near 95 per dollar as RBI measures support it
items.summary: TradingView and other market reports put the rupee around 94.90 to 95.30 per dollar, recovering from about 96.79 earlier, helped by RBI curbs on rebooking cancelled forex derivatives and a special FX window for state refiners. Analysts still expect pressure, with S&P Global seeing about 97 by end-2026. Nothing specific to 3 November turned up, so figures are provisional.
items.why: A weak rupee raises the cost of imports and overseas education and squeezes company margins.

items.title: Sensex up 1.7% to about 75,693 and Nifty near 23,441 on 2 November, a third straight gain
items.summary: Business Standard and Kotak Neo report the Sensex closing around 75,692.78 and the Nifty 50 around 23,440, both up about 1.7%, with Reliance Industries jumping 12% on results and lower crude helping. One data site shows a different Sensex level, likely an earlier-session figure, so the numbers are provisional.
items.why: Rising markets lift recruiters' risk appetite and campus-hiring plans.

items.title: Oil fell sharply on Monday on hopes of a Gulf deal
items.summary: One summary says oil dropped more than 7% on Monday, while a market report says crude was down more than 2% in early Indian trade. The sources differ on size, so treat the move as provisional.
items.why: Oil prices shape India's inflation, rupee and corporate costs.

items.title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing raises its Google hosting commitment to about 121 billion dollars
items.summary: A 2 November AI roundup reports the amended filing lifts Anthropic's minimum spend under a Google hosting agreement to about 121.3 billion dollars through July 2033, and says it expects to pay SpaceX's AI unit about 3.1 billion dollars a month from December 2026. The detail comes from an aggregator, so it is provisional.
items.why: Shows how AI vendors' infrastructure bills shape pricing and the tools employers adopt.

items.title: OpenAI funding reports still conflict, and it announced four Abu Dhabi agreements
items.summary: One source says OpenAI trimmed its round to 20 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion valuation, another that it secured about 11 billion in commitments against a 30 billion target. A separate report lists four OpenAI agreements announced in Abu Dhabi on 2 November. Figures conflict, so all are provisional.
items.why: Investor appetite decides which AI vendors employers can rely on.

items.title: Apple reportedly testing Alibaba's Qwen in Apple Intelligence for China
items.summary: Aggregator feeds report Apple is starting tests of Apple Intelligence in China using Alibaba's Qwen model. This is unconfirmed by a primary source.
items.why: Local AI partnerships show how global brands adapt products to regulated markets.
